_comment: The 7-stage PR-gated pipeline expressed as actions — workflow #1.
There is no workflow file at runtime: the workflow IS this set of actions.
Nothing here knows about any other action; the coupling is the board.
Two topics carry the story, and keeping them apart is the whole trick:
cadre/stages/<story>  — SESSION lifecycle. A stage session (or the
cadre/github/<story>  — REPO state, put on the board by the gh-watch
GitHub is reached by an action running a CLI;
A contracts SESSION finishing is not a contract PR MERGING — the first
opens the PR, the second advances the machine. pipeline.py conflates
neither, and neither does this file.
all-built assembly check, _try_automerge's risk-high hold, and the reap-side

actions.name: gh-watch
actions._why: The daemon writes one heartbeat per poll pass; this turns it into a repo read. The shim writes the pr-state, risk and summon events directly to the board — one command, many events, which no single emitter could express.

actions.name: story-to-intake
actions._why: S0. Reproduces _begin_intake: a registered story with no run yet gets an intake session. `no_event_for_key` on the stage signal is the once-only guard — pipeline.py gets the same effect from runs.key_active.

actions.name: intake-finished-awaits-plan
actions._why: Reproduces _finish_intake's tail: the planning PR now exists and the story sits in phase `interrogate` waiting for a human to merge it. No spawn — the next move belongs to the driver, and gh-watch is what notices when they make it.

payload.note: planning PR open — awaiting driver merge

actions.name: planning-merged-to-contracts
actions._why: dispatcher.dispatch, pr_merged/planning, legacy branch: the manifest declares a contract node, so the separate contracts stage still runs. gh_watch reads the manifest off the planning PR body and stamps `flow` — the closed `where` vocabulary cannot reach into a PR body, so the classification rides in the payload.

actions.name: planning-merged-to-slices
actions._why: dispatcher.dispatch -> {type: phase_slices}: the unified-spec flow (2026-08-26). No slice's flow carries a contract node, so the approved spec IS the contract — flip the phase and let the slice actions fire.

actions.name: slice-ready-to-tests
actions._why: dispatcher.ready_actions' hole-filler: in the contract-less flow there is no contract merge for tests to chain off (the spec IS the contract), so gh_watch emits `ready` for a stage whose predecessor is flow-exempt. First engine-only run stalled at phase->slices without this (2026-09-11).

actions.name: slice-ready-to-build
actions._why: Same hole-filler as slice-ready-to-tests, for a flow whose slice skips the tests node — build would otherwise wait on a tests merge that can never happen.

actions.name: contract-merged-to-tests
actions._why: dispatcher.dispatch, pr_merged/contract -> run_stage tests for that slice.

actions.name: tests-merged-to-build
actions._why: dispatcher.dispatch, pr_merged/tests -> run_stage build. The tests PR merging is what locks the tests; the builder is forbidden from touching them.

actions.name: build-merged-slice-done
actions._why: dispatcher.dispatch, pr_merged/build -> {type: noop, built: slice}. The slice is done; whether the STORY is done is an aggregate over the manifest, which gh_watch evaluates (dispatcher.all_built) and reports as its own event.

actions.name: all-built-to-assembly
actions._why: Reproduces _poll_story's tail: dispatcher.all_built(story, open_prs) and phase == slices -> run_stage assembly on the planning PR.

actions.name: assembly-finished-to-final-review
actions._why: Reproduces _reap_runs' assembly branch: phase -> final-review and the session's own briefing goes in front of the driver. Final review is the second legitimate surface (driver decision 2026-08-30) — the assembly session authored it; the pipeline only opens it.

emitter.summary: Final review: story {payload[story]} is assembled — merge the final PR to ship it

actions.name: final-merged-story-done
actions._why: dispatcher.dispatch, pr_merged/final -> {type: story_done}. The human merging the story PR is the act that ships it; nothing downstream fires.

actions.name: risk-high-to-triage
actions._why: _try_automerge's risk-high branch (cadre-context 2026-08-23: risk gates merge, confidence ranks). A hold is a DECISION to make, not a PR to read, so a second independent assessor audits the grade and authors the driver's brief. gh_watch stamps the grade off the PR body; the merge block itself stays in automerge.decide.

actions.name: conflict-to-reconcile
actions._why: _maybe_reconcile: a conflicted pipeline PR gets a reconcile run rather than waiting for a human untangle. The rounds cap that escalates after N attempts is NOT expressible here — see the report; the engine's causal-depth cap is the only loop guard this action carries.

actions.name: summon-to-interrogate
actions._why: dispatcher.dispatch, summon on the planning PR -> run_stage interrogate. The round cap (limits.max_rounds_per_stage) lives in the daemon, not here.

actions.name: summon-to-revise
actions._why: dispatcher.dispatch, summon on a contract/tests/build/final PR -> run_stage revise. A summon on a CLOSED PR buys nothing (`Closing, superseded by X` is a normal thing to write) — gh_watch drops those before they reach the board.

actions.name: stage-failed-to-driver
actions._why: _reap_runs' failure tail (the '⚠️ Stage run failed' comment) plus the engine's own failure-as-a-signal: a body or emitter that blows up writes `signal: failed`, and triage is an ordinary action (round 4). Both land here.
actions._note: The summary reads only header fields. An engine-authored failure signal carries {status, action, error, trigger_event} and NOT {stage, story} — templating those here would fail the hitl emitter, which would write another failed signal, which is exactly the loop the depth cap exists to stop. Say less, always render.

emitter.summary: A pipeline stage failed on {event[key]} — check the runner logs, then re-summon

actions.name: escalated-to-driver
actions._why: An escalation is a decision handed back to the driver. In engine-only mode the round caps are enforced at the spawn seam (engine_seam.refuse_past_cap) and refuse by writing `escalate` — without this action that write would sit on the board unread, which is the silent wedge the cap exists to prevent. Same summary discipline as stage-failed-to-driver: header fields only, so it always renders.
